A passes all 10 checks, but its fidelity drops to 0.787, below the raw input's 0.841. That fits its heavy processing: two afftdn passes at nr=30, a 10 kHz low-pass, a gate that cuts pauses by about 30 dB, and added pink noise, which is the underwater, over-processed sound the brief warned against. B gets the best fidelity (0.868) and the cleanest hum removal (0.7 dB vs 3.1 dB) from lighter, more sensible filters. Its one failure is levels_evened: the quiet passages come up from -8.4 dB to -4.4 dB, while A reaches -2.4 dB. That's a real shortfall, but a smaller sin than degrading the voice.

B ducks the music 21.1 dB under the voice (voice-to-music 22.5 dB) and scored higher on voice fidelity (0.961), while A ducks only 9.4 dB with a sidechain compressor at ratio 6, which is weaker than the brief's 'well below the voice' and puts intelligibility more at risk. B also sets the music level from the measured loudness of both files and builds a smooth gain curve from detected pauses, so it adapts to other inputs and returns the music in the gaps between sentences. A uses a fixed -20 dB bed cut and a fixed silence threshold that only suit this pair of files. B's tail is also correct: it fades over the 4 seconds that end 4 s after the last word, while A adds a 0.5 s swell before its 4 s fade, so its tail runs about 4.5 s.

A ducks the music much more (21.1 dB vs 9.4 dB) and keeps the voice further above it (22.5 vs 17.2 dB voice-to-music). It also scores higher on voice fidelity, so the words stay clearer. A sets the music level from the measured loudness of both files and builds the duck from detected pauses, so it adapts to other recordings. B uses a fixed -20 dB cut on the music and a mild 6:1 sidechain compressor, which only fits this one file. A's music bed sits above the voice (voice-to-music -3.5 dB, only 5.5 dB of ducking). That fails the ducks, voice_above_music and voice_intact checks and would make the spot hard to understand on AM. B gain-stages the music relative to the voice's loudness and ducks it 16 dB with a timed gain curve that ramps down before each line and back up after, so it passes all 13 checks and keeps the voice clean (fidelity 0.933 vs 0.588). B also trims each line's silence and fades the bed and sting out, so it ends cleaner (-59.7 dB vs -31.1 dB). A's sting runs right up to the end with only a 0.1 s fade.

B's sidechain compressor at threshold 0.03 and ratio 4 ducks the bed by only 5.5 dB. That leaves the music 3.5 dB louder than the voice, and voice fidelity drops to 0.588, so it fails the ducks, voice_above_music and voice_intact checks. That is unusable for an AM spot where the words have to come through. A trims silence from each line, places the lines from where the speech actually starts, and uses a deterministic 16 dB duck curve with smooth ramps, which gives a 22.8 dB voice-to-music margin and an end tail at -60 dB. B also ends on a 0.1 s fade that leaves the tail at -31 dB, so the ending is much less clean.
